songs.title: the hour is wide open
songs.description: Soul pop for a cafe, B flat major, 90 BPM. Female low alto, half voice, near speech, as if humming to herself, behind the beat. Narrow melody in a fourth, one phrase returning; the chorus keeps those notes and lifts because the band opens, not because she pushes; lines end early. Rounded consonants, almost no vibrato. Full band, dense and soft: low phased Rhodes, three-note motif, struck short; muted electric guitar chopping off-beats; one harmony voice, last chorus, no choir; deep round bass, short; cross-stick, low tom, dark shaker every bar, never dropping out. Harmony Bbmaj9 - Bbm9 - Ebmaj9 - F9 to Bbmaj9, home turning minor for one bar. Vocals behind the band, blended in, not upfront. Dark warm tone, highs rolled off, lo-fi. Ends on a plucked chord, about two and a half minutes, the lyric filling all of it. One note per syllable, the band carrying every lift. No melisma, no sustained high notes, no head voice, no saxophone, no smoky bar or lounge, no autotune, no pop gloss.

songs.title: Let the Water Keep It
songs.description: Free rhythm timed by breathing: a short phrase, then a stop, then the room goes quiet. One solo daegeum, a large Korean bamboo transverse flute, in its low register. Each phrase is softer and lower than the one before, until only breath is left. Only five pitches in the whole piece: B flat, C, D, F, G. No other notes, no augmented second, no bent quarter tones. Air enters before the tone, no tonguing, membrane buzz almost absent. Close and dry, one mic in a small wooden room, short tail, nothing held underneath, only room tone in the gaps. Every phrase settles on the low B flat; at the end of a long tone the pitch falls slowly to the next note of the scale. The figure returns, never the same length twice. Sleep music. No vocals. One instrument alone: no ensemble, no second instrument, no percussion, no piano, no guitar, no strings, no synth, no pad, no drone. No rain, no nature sounds. No crescendo, no climax.

No other notes, no augmented second, no bent quarter tones. Air enters each note slowly, no tonguing, membrane buzz almost absent, one slow wide fall at the very end of a long tone. Close and dry, one mic in a small wooden room, short tail, nothing held underneath, only room tone in the gaps. Every phrase settles on the low B flat; the last note is held until it sags. The figure returns, never the same length twice. Sleep music. No vocals. One instrument alone: no ensemble, no second instrument, no percussion, no piano, no guitar, no strings, no synth, no pad, no drone. No rain, no nature sounds. No crescendo, no climax.

songs.title: 잡아 줄래
songs.description: Early-2000s Korean warm bright pop, sung in Korean by a bright male mid-range voice, B3 to E4, sincere, no female vocals, never belted, never strained, no rasp. B flat major, 98 BPM, gently rocking like a boat. A clean electric guitar leads with a light fingerpicked pattern, a solo cello answering between lines with a warm singing counter-melody. Light kit: cajon, shaker, soft rim clicks. Small close-miked strings, airy and sweet. Each chorus line steps through a bright passing chord before landing home, the one bright event. Warm smiling delivery, slightly behind the beat, small vibrato at line ends only, no crescendo. The voice carries every line to the end, no long instrumental tail. The backing track has a dark top end with no cymbal sizzle. The voice keeps its natural breath and air, close-miked and present. Lead vocal clearly in front of the band. No English lyrics, no autotune, no trot, no K-pop gloss, no sad cello solo. Bright airy modern mix, not retro.
